name: Decide ceiling increase requests
description: Applies when asked to settle a limit-increase (ceiling) request for an account, where a standing rule and an approvable cap govern the outcome.
procedure:
- Fetch the case details to get the account, requested limit, and status.
- Fetch the account details to check verification, standing, tenure, and current limit.
- Read the policy section on limits for the standing rule and the approvable cap.
- Apply the standing rule first: an account with bad standing (e.g. recent chargeback) is denied with the standing reason, regardless of amount.
- Otherwise approve if the requested limit is within the cap; if above the cap, deny with the cap-exceeded reason.
check: Before submitting, re-derive the decision from the policy text: confirm which rule fires (standing vs cap) and that the reason code submitted matches that rule; re-read the account's standing field rather than relying on memory.
known_bad: Approving a limit-increase request for an account with bad standing merely because the requested amount is under the documented cap; the re-derivation shows the standing rule fires first and the check fails.

name: Decide flagged transfer cases
description: Applies when asked to decide a flagged outbound (or inbound) transfer case between an account and a payee, where screening must rely on the payee record because the restricted-payee roster is not published, and the reporting threshold must be read from the transfers policy.
procedure:
- Fetch the case details, then the account and payee details in parallel.
- Read the transfers policy section for the reporting threshold and restricted-payee rules in force.
- Treat the payee record (name, type, jurisdiction, any restriction flags) as the screening signal, since roster entries are unpublished and no other screen may be available.
- Compare the amount against the documented reporting threshold; escalate with `reportable_amount` if it is above the threshold.
- Deny with `restricted_payee` only when the payee record or the case itself indicates a restriction.
- Do not block on account standing or tenure; established practice is that they do not gate transfers.
- Approve when the amount is under the threshold and no restriction is indicated.
check: Before deciding, re-read the transfers policy section and recompute the amount against the documented threshold; confirm the payee record was actually fetched and reviewed for restriction signals rather than assumed clean.
known_bad: A transfer whose amount exceeds the documented reporting threshold, approved without escalation: the recomputation in the check exceeds the threshold, so the decision must instead be an escalation with reason `reportable_amount`.

name: Settle pending card transactions
description: Applies when asked to decide a pending card transaction (card queue entry) for a charge at a merchant on an account, where the documented category instant-approve limit may be out of date and scored run evidence establishes how far the limit in force extends.
procedure:
- Gather the case, account, merchant, and the transactions policy section.
- If the amount is at or below the documented category limit, approve (checking standing and any region/category restrictions).
- If the amount exceeds the documented limit, search the skill library for a scored run result in the same category where escalating a charge at some amount B was scored wrong; treat that as proof the limit in force is at least B.
- Approve when the charge amount is at or below the recorded bound B; escalate with reason over_limit when the amount is above B.
- Never extend approval past the recorded bound: prior evidence bounds the limit from below only up to the amount actually tested.
check: Recompute the comparison: confirm the charge amount is at or below a recorded bound B that comes from an actual scored result (an escalation at B scored wrong), not from documentation alone; if the amount is above every recorded bound, an approval must not be trusted.
known_bad: A charge above the documented category limit where the only recorded bound in the library is smaller than the charge amount: approving it fails the check, because the effective limit may sit between the recorded bound and the charge.

name: Decide card transaction cases
description: Applies when asked to decide a pending card transaction (card queue entry) for a charge at a merchant on an account, where the documented category instant-approve limit may be out of date and recorded scored-run evidence about the limit in force takes precedence over the documentation.
procedure:
- Fetch the case, the account, and the merchant in parallel to get amount, category, standing, and merchant details.
- Read the transactions policy section for the documented category instant-approve limits.
- Treat the documented limit as possibly out of date: before escalating for over_limit, check recorded scored-run evidence for that category.
- For electronics, recorded evidence shows the limit in force extends to at least $611.25 (an electronics charge of $611.25 was wrongly escalated in a prior scored run, and an approval below that bound scored correct), so treat the effective electronics instant-approve limit as at least $611.25 despite a documented $500.
- If the amount is at or below the highest recorded approvable bound for the category, approve; if it exceeds that bound, escalate with the documented reason (for example over_limit).
- Categories without a listed limit have no amount restriction, gift cards are available to all tiers, and no category is restricted by merchant region.
check: Recompute the decision against the highest recorded approvable bound for the category before acting: approve only if amount <= that bound, escalate only if amount > that bound; confirm the bound comes from scored-run evidence rather than the possibly outdated documented limit.
known_bad: An electronics charge above the documented $500 limit but below the recorded $611.25 bound, such as a $540 electronics charge, would be escalated as over_limit by the documented rule alone; the check fails because the recorded bound shows the limit in force covers it and it must be approved.
